content.text: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod. My name is Marco.

content.text: My name is Catherine and today we have a very technical, very advanced lesson for you.
content.trans: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们要进行一次非常技术且先进的课程。

content.text: This is all about one of my favorite subjects.

content.trans:
好的。我们接下来要聊音乐，但是我们要具体聊聊的是关于

好的，我们稍等一下。一会儿我们就回来，这次我们要聊的是关于

content.text: what these words and phrases mean.

content.text: Hi Cody, how did practicing go this week?
content.trans: 你好，柯迪，这一周的练习怎么样？

content.trans: 哎，这一周我有几个测试和一次口试，所以没时间背诵了

content.text: the second page, but I think I'm asked through the tricky section.

content.text: Great. Warm up with some scales in arpeggios first.
content.trans: 好的。先用和弦练习暖身一下吧。

content.text: Good, good. This week we're going to keep the rhythm steady when you play the last part
content.trans: 好的，好的。这周我们来保持节奏稳定，你最后的部分要继续哦！

content.text: with the 16th notes. Now let's take a look at this tricky section.
content.trans: 第十六节来了。我们现在来看看这个 tricky 的部分。

content.text: Charlene, before I start, I was wondering if it was okay if I put a small crescendo in
content.trans: Charlene，先说一下，我打算在开始前，想问一下你如果可以的话，是否可以小声一点？这样我就不会把声音太大了。

content.text: here and then a D crescendo back to pianissimo again over here.
content.trans: 然后这里和那里，D号渐强后又回到pp（极弱）了。

content.text: Hmm, it might work. I'll have to hear it. Show me what you've done.
content.trans: 嗯，或许有效。我得听听看。给我看看你做了什么。

content.text: Not bad.
content.trans: 不错。

content.text: It was horrible. I played it much better at home.
content.trans: 确实挺糟糕的。在家里玩的时候，我表现得更好了。

content.text: It's just nerves. Just play the right hand for now.
content.trans: 这只是一个紧张。现在就只弹右手吧。

content.text: One, two, three, four, five, six, ta, ti, triple, ti. Good, good.
content.trans: 一，二，三，四，五，六，太，的士，三倍，的士。好，好。

content.text: Don't forget the accidentals. The key signature says that note should be a G sharp, but now it's
content.trans: 不要忘记小错误。乐谱上说这个音符应该是大调的G#，但现在它是小调的G#.

content.text: a G natural. Now add the bass clef. Oh, you're going too fast.
content.trans: 一个G大调。现在加上低音谱号。哦，你太快了。

content.text: Remember the tempo for this piece is andante.
content.trans: 记得这首曲子的节奏是慢板。

content.text: Is that better? Yes, much better. Watch where you lift your foot off the pedal. What was that?
content.trans: 那是不是更好？是的，好多了。看看你踩油门的时候脚抬起来的地方。那是怎么回事？

content.text: Sorry, the stretch for that octave is always hard to make.
content.trans: 对不起，那个八度的延音总是很难做出。

content.text: That's okay. Keep going. You're moving ahead by leaps and bounds. Watch your dynamics.
content.trans: 好的。继续吧。你正在快速前进。注意你的动态。

content.text: Keep your elbows lifted. Remember to stroke the keys. Don't pound. That's better.
content.trans: 请抬起你的肘部。记得敲击键盘。不要用力敲打。这样更好。

content.text: Remember that as a pianist or any other musician, your technique will be what separates you from the pack just as much or as more so as your
content.trans: 记得，作为钢琴家或者其他音乐家，你的技巧将成为你区别于他人的重要因素，甚至比之更多。

content.text: musicianship.
content.trans: 音乐才华

content.text: All right, we're back. So you probably noticed that there are a lot of ways to describe certain aspects of playing the piano.
content.trans: 好的，我们回来了。你大概注意到了有很多方式可以描述弹钢琴的一些方面吧。

content.text: They talked about scales and all that stuff. So why don't we take a deeper look at this vocab in language, take away part one.
content.trans: 他们讨论了秤和所有这些内容。那我们为什么不深入了解一下这个词汇在语言中的运用，去掉一部分呢？

content.text: Language take away.
content.trans: 语言带走。

content.text: Okay, so the first part of the lesson is the warm-up. That's when we start to get our fingers moving and really stretch out.
content.trans: 好的，课程的第一部分是热身。那是我们开始动起来的时候，也是真的伸个懒腰的时候。

content.text: This is an important part of any musician's routine because it's also a way to practice some very basic, very fundamental things for the first of which is a scale.
content.trans: 这是一支音乐家日常routine的一部分，也是练习一些非常基本、非常基础的东西的一种方式。其中的第一个是调式。

content.text: Okay, so actually Cody started warming up with some scales. So what exactly are scales?
content.trans: 好的，所以其实科迪已经开始练指法了。那么什么是指法呢？

content.text: Well, basically there are different musical notes. Some people know them as do re mi fa solatido. Some people call them C-D-E-F-G-A-B-C.
content.trans: 嗯，基本上有不同类型的音符。有些人叫它们do re mi fa solatido。有些则称为C-D-E-F-G-A-B-C。

content.text: But each of those and many others have scales. So that's eight notes together.
content.trans: 但这些和许多其他人都有分量。所以，八下就是这么回事儿。

content.text: Okay, so basically when you're playing scales, you're just playing a sequence of these eight notes.
content.trans: 好的，当你弹奏八度音阶时，你只是在演奏这些八度的序列。

content.text: Right, going up or down.
content.trans: 好的，上还是下。

content.text: Okay, to warm up. And what about in our Pagio? I think this is Italian, right?
content.trans: 好的，热身一下。我们Pagio那边呢？我觉得这是意大利语吧？

content.text: Definitely. Our Pagio is another kind of warm-up where you're not playing every single note. You're playing some notes in a scale.
content.trans: 当然。我们的Pagio是一种不同于一般的暖身练习，你不会演奏每一条线上的每一个音符。你会在某个音阶上演奏一些音符。

content.text: Right, so da da da da da da da da da da. That's an arpeggio.
content.trans: 好的，所以哒哒哒哒哒哒哒哒哒哒。那是一个琶音。

content.text: Okay, very good. So, and as you said, these are usually for warm-ups, right?
content.trans: 好的，很好。所以，正如你所说，这些通常是热身用的，对吧？

content.text: Yeah, they're also very important because they come in to play later when you're talking about the key that a song or piece of music is in.
content.trans: 没错，它们也很重要，因为它们会在你谈论歌曲或音乐的主调时出现。

content.text: So this helps you memorize the key that some music is in.
content.trans: 所以这能帮助你记住一些音乐的调子。

content.text: Okay, very good. So I think related to this is the rhythm of the piece that you're playing.
content.trans: 好的，很好。我觉得这和你演奏的曲子的节奏有关。

content.text: That's right. So rhythm is really important. Some people can even say, you know, he's got rhythm or they have rhythm.
content.trans: 没错。所以节奏真的很重要。有些人甚至可以说，你知道，他有节奏或者他们有节奏。

content.text: It's a way to describe the beat of a kind of music. So sometimes it has to do with how fast or how slow something is.
content.trans: 这是一个用来描述一种音乐节拍的方式。有时候，它与某事物的速度或速度有关。

content.text: Other times it has to do with the way that the notes work together.
content.trans: 其他时候，它与笔记如何协同工作有关。

content.text: For example, a steady beat would be 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4.
This is a complicated beat. It goes ta ti trippoli ta ti trippoli. So this is a very difficult kind of rhythm.
content.trans: 这是一个复杂的节奏。它走着，穿过提里奥普利特，再走过提里奥普利特。所以这是一种非常困难的节奏。

content.text: Okay, so the rhythm is just kind of, it gives you the how fast, how slow it is.
content.trans: 好的，节奏就是那种感觉，它让你知道快慢的程度。

content.text: And I guess if you can take a look at notes and you can play it in many different rhythms, but not necessarily they're going to sound correct.
content.trans: 当然，如果你可以看看笔记，并且可以在不同的节奏中演奏，但不一定非要听起来正确。

content.text: Right. And actually it's interesting. In English we also have a group of instruments that are called rhythm instruments.
content.trans: 没错。而且实际上挺有意思的。我们英语里也有一个叫节奏乐器的群体。

content.text: So this would be like the drums. Okay, so it gives the beat. Yes. Very good. And while moving on, I think some other Italian words popped up in here when they talked about crescendo and decrescendo.
content.trans: 英语：所以这就像节奏鼓。嗯，它给了节奏感。是的。很好。而当我在继续时，我注意到这里可能在谈论升和降。

content.text: Right. So crescendo is when something becomes louder. So I can make a crescendo.
content.trans: 好的。所以crescendo就是指某样东西变大声了。我可以让它变大声。

content.text: Right. But a decrescendo, day in Italian, just like in English means it's the opposite. So it means it's getting really softer.
content.trans: 好的。但是一段缓降，意大利语的 giorno 和英语中的 day 一样，意思是它变得越来越柔和了。

content.text: Okay. And what about pianissimo?
content.trans: 好的。钢琴弱吗？

content.text: Pianissimo is basically an indication. It also comes from Italian. It's an indication that a player, a musician should play something very, very, very quietly.
content.trans: “柔板”基本上是一个指示。它也源自意大利语。这是一个演奏者，一个音乐家应该演奏得非常、非常、非常安静的指示。

content.text: Okay. It's almost like a whisper.
content.trans: 好的。感觉就像是低语一样。

content.text: Okay. So all these three words have to do with the volume of or how loud or not so loud you play the instrument.
content.trans: 好的。这三句话都是关于你演奏乐器时的音量大小、声音的强弱或者是否足够强。

content.text: That's right. Okay. Very good. And well, moving on now, we talk about accidentals.
content.trans: 没错。很好。好的，那我们现在来说说意外吧。

content.text: Okay. This is important. Remember earlier we were talking about scales. Well, for example, the G scale has one sharp.
content.trans: 好的。这是重要的。记得之前我们提到过尺子。比如，G调有半音。

content.text: So that's an F sharp. So if I'm playing it on the piano, there are seven white keys and one black key.
content.trans: 所以这是F大调。如果我在钢琴上弹奏，有七个白键和一个黑键。

content.text: Okay. So actually here they mentioned G sharp and then something like G natural. All these, just like for everyone that's out there is complete Chinese.
content.trans: 好的。所以实际上这里提到的是大调G和然后是自然G，就像对所有人来说都是完整的中文。

content.text: We have no idea what this is all about. So you have the accidentals and G sharp and you're describing something about sharpness with accidentals.
content.trans: 我们完全不知道这是怎么回事。所以你有大调和升G，你在描述用装饰音带来的锐度。

content.text: That's right. So basically if you look at a piano, you have white keys. Those are natural. So they don't have a sharp or flat.
content.trans: 对。那么，如果你看看钢琴，你会看到有白键。那都是自然的。所以它们没有强弱标记。

content.text: The sharp and flats are actually played on the black keys. Usually it's a half step from a normal note. So G, it's a half step.
content.trans:
琴键上的尖和平其实是放在黑键上。通常来说，一个正常的音符后面是一个半音。
G 是半音。

content.text: We're talking about different keys. So if something is in the key of G, in all the music people, no, this is key of G, there's one accidental.
content.trans: 我们正在讨论不同的键。所以如果某个键在G上，那么所有音乐人都知道这个键是G的。

content.text: What's the accidental? It's always F sharp. And so an accidental means a sharp or a flat in that key.
content.trans: 什么的意外？总是F大调。因此，一个音符意味着是半音还是全音就取决于那个调。

content.text: Okay. And when we talk about sharps on the piano, they're basically the black keys. Yes. Well, sharps and flats can both be black keys.
content.trans: 好的。当我们谈论钢琴上的锐角时，它们实际上是黑键。是的，尖和扁都可以是黑键。

content.text: Very good. And well, apart from accidentals and G sharp, G natural, the teacher also talked about a bass clef.
content.trans: 很好。除了意外和G大调，老师还讲了低音谱号。

content.text: Okay. This is important for people who play lower instruments like the bass, you know, the upright bass.
content.trans: 好的。这是对低音提琴这类像贝斯这样的乐器演奏者很重要的事情，你知道的，就是那把直立式贝斯。

content.text: That big one or people who play the piano, obviously, this represents a way of writing the lower notes. Okay.
content.trans: 那大一点的，或者会弹钢琴的人，显然这是在写低音的一种方式。好了。

content.text: Okay. So you see the lines, those five lines on paper and people write the notes. Well, sometimes they're for higher instruments, you know, the flute or the trumpet.
content.trans: 好的。你看到的线条，就是纸上的五条线和人们写在纸上的字。有时候这些是高级仪器，比如小提琴或大提琴。

content.text: But sometimes when they're for lower instruments, like the left hand of a piano or for the upright bass, you have to write it in a special register, a special part of the sound kind of continuum.
content.trans: 但是有时候，当他们用于低档乐器时，比如钢琴的左手或竖琴的正位，你必须在特定的区域写一个特殊的标记，这个区域是声乐和连续音域的一部分。

content.text: And that's the treble. That's the bass clef. Okay. So basically, if anyone has ever seen piano notes, it tells you what to play with your left hand.
content.trans: 没错。反正，只要见过钢琴谱上的音符，就知道用左手弹什么了。

content.text: And you're right hand. So I imagine the bass clef will be everything that's on your left hand because that sounds like deeper, graver, right?
content.trans: 你就是我的右手。所以我想，低音谱号应该是你的左手的所有内容吧，听起来更深沉、更有力呢？

content.text: Yeah, it's lower. So it's lower on the scale instead of like up high up here where it's on the treble clef.
content.trans: 没错，它就低一些。所以它是比这里高处的音符要低一些，而不是像在高位置上。

content.text: All right. So the opposite would be the treble clef. That's right. The treble clef is up higher. It's most other instruments like the trumpet.
content.trans: 好的。所以反面就是小指谱。对的。小指谱比其他乐器高，比如长笛。

content.text: The bass clef is for lower instruments. And it just means that the way that you read the music on the page is a little bit different.
content.trans: 低音谱号用于低音乐器。只是说你在乐谱上阅读的方式稍微有点不同。

content.text: Okay. Very good. And well, we also got into things like tempo and the piece was described as andante.
content.trans: 好的。太棒了。而且我们也谈到了节拍，那个片段被描述为安可（ante'）的。

content.text: Andante. This is a very Italian word. Okay. So andante means that something is played slowly.
content.trans: Andante。这是一个非常意大利的词。好的。所以和弦的意思是，某件事情被演奏得缓慢。

content.text: Okay. So apart from andante, if so it's a style or a tempo. I guess tempo is the speed of which is played, right?
content.trans: 好的。除了Andante之外，如果还有的话，那就是风格或速度了。我觉得速度是演奏的速度，对吧？

content.text: But in you're right to say that it's also a style because in many symphonies, for example, there's a movement, a part of the symphony that's called the andante.
content.trans: 但是你说到这也是风格确实是的，在许多交响乐中，例如有一部分交响曲叫做“行板”。

content.text: And that's when everything starts to get slow and serious or pretty.
content.trans: 那才是时候一切都开始变得缓慢而严肃或者挺好的。

content.text: I've heard, I don't know, in piano, I've heard of something called staccato. And I think this is also related to tempo, right?
content.trans: 我听说过，我不太知道，在钢琴上，我会听到叫做“断奏”的东西。我认为这也是与速度有关的。

content.text: Staccato is the way that you play something. So instead of having these long, pretty notes, you're playing them like this.
content.trans: 顿挫就是你演奏的方式。所以，而不是有这些长长的、漂亮的音符，你是在演奏这个样子的。

content.text: Not a very very sharp. Right, like a machine gun. But it's not related to the tempo. It's kind of more just like the way that you press the keys.
content.trans: 不是特别锐利。对，就像机关枪一样。但和节奏没关系。更多就是你按键的感觉。

content.text: Exactly. It's a style for playing.
content.trans: 确实。这是一个玩的游戏风格。

content.text: Okay. All right. Well, the teacher also told the student to be careful where they lift the foot off the pedal. And the students said,
content.trans: 好的。好的。老师也告诉学生，脚离开踏板的时候要小心点。学生们说，

content.text: the so sorry, the stretch for that octave is always hard to make.
content.trans: 真的很抱歉，那个八度的延长时间总是很难。

content.text: Okay. So an octave is really really important in music. Like we were talking about earlier with the scale, a scale is eight notes.
content.trans: 好的。所以八度在音乐中真的非常重要。就像我们之前提到的，音阶由八个音组成。

content.text: Well, the root, the place the word octave comes from is the number eight, like an octagon.
content.trans: 嗯，八度音阶的根源在于数字8，就像一个正方形。

content.text: Right. So octave means eight notes together or like low C. High C, that's an octave.
content.trans: 好的。所以八度就是指八度音程，或者说是低C到高C。高C，那就是一个八度。

content.text: Okay. So think about the piano when you're putting your fingers on the keys, covering eight keys means you have to stretch your thumb and you're pinky out really, really far.
content.trans: 好的。所以当你按键盘上的八键时，你得把拇指和食指伸直，而且你的中指要远远地伸出。

content.text: And so he's saying, sorry, it's hard for me to do this because the octave that that stretch is really hard for my hair.
content.trans: 所以他说，对不起，这对我来说真的很难做，因为那个伸展真的很对我的头发不好。

content.text: Right. Okay. So this is different from an eighth, right?
content.trans: 好的。对了，这和第八不一样呢？

content.text: Well, it depends on your time. I don't know because it just came into my because an octave is eight and an eighth note.
content.trans: 好吧，取决于你的时间。我没有知道，因为刚刚它才进入我的耳朵，一个八度是八，一个八分音符。

content.text: It's a different, I imagine. Yeah. Well, you heard in the dialogue, 16th note, eighth note.
content.trans: 听起来是不一样的，我想。对了。你记得在对话里听到的十六分音符和八分音符吧？

content.text: That's actually talking about the length of a note. How long you hold it?
content.trans: 那其实是在说信的长度。你写多长？

content.text: Okay. So basically you're saying it's the way you measure the music.
content.trans: 好的。所以你意思是说，这是衡量音乐的方式。

content.text: You can have four count or three count, but you divide that into pieces.
content.trans: 你可以有四件，或者三件，但你把它分成几块。

content.text: It's like a pie in math where you divide it into pieces. So if it's a 16th note or an eighth note, that's the length based on the kind of music you're playing.
content.trans: 英语：它就像数学中的一个蛋糕，你把它的部分切成几块。如果是一十六分音符或八分音符，那么这个长度就是根据你所演奏的音乐类型来确定的。

content.text: So I imagine 16th note is shorter than eighth. Yes. Okay. At least I got that one.
content.trans: 所以我想16分音符比八分音符短，是的。好的。至少我得到了这一点。

content.text: And 32nd note is shorter than a 16th note. Wow. You have all the way up to 34th note.
content.trans: 第32小节比十六分音符短。哇塞，你有从三十四小节到全部的小节都唱完的可能。

content.text: 64th note is short. Okay. It gets very complicated, very mathy.
content.trans: 第64个音节很短。好的。这变得非常复杂，非常数学化。

content.text: All right. And towards the end of the teacher recommended for Cody to watch his dynamics.
content.trans: 好的。老师推荐 Cody 看他的动态。

content.text: What does she mean with watch your dynamics? I used to get this all the time in music.
content.trans: 她这是在说“动态”吗？以前音乐里经常用到这个词。

content.text: So you're concentrating on your music. You're playing. You're getting the notes and Cody is stretching his hands.
content.trans: 你专注于你的音乐。你在弹奏。你在练习和Cody的手在伸展。

content.text: The octaves are so far away and he forgets to play it loud or soft.
content.trans: 这音阶那么远，他总是忘了开多大声或者小声。

content.text: Oh, okay. Because on the page it says like we heard earlier, day crescendo.
content.trans: 哦，好的。因为页面上说的就像我们之前听过的那样，高潮迭起。

content.text: So get much, much softer. So Cody completely forgot.
content.trans: 所以要很软很多。所以科迪完全忘了。

content.text: He's not listening. He's not reading the page and seeing what it says about the volume of the music.
content.trans: 他没在听。他没有看那一页，也不看里面关于音乐的量说了什么。

content.text: So basically the dynamics are like the instructions of how loud to play it or not or not so loud.
content.trans: 所以基本上就是动态就像播放的指令一样，是大点声音就放，不放或者小一点的声音。

content.text: Exactly. So it doesn't say pianissimo or the opposite. Does it say forte?
content.trans: 没错。它没说如极弱、强这样的词。说的对不？

content.text: So it actually say this on the notes in forte. I'll say that.
content.trans: 所以笔记上确实写着这个。我来告诉你。

content.text: F-O-R-T-E or sometimes just F.
content.trans: F-O-R-T-E 或者有时候只是 F。

content.text: So P is piano. That means like we said earlier, quiet.
content.trans: 所以 P 是钢琴。那意味着我们之前说过的，安静。

content.text: Pianissimo is P-P-P. It's very quiet. F is forte. Loud.
content.trans: 小提琴很轻柔，就是P-P-P。非常安静。力度大就是F-F-F。声音很大。

content.text: Okay. So I think if anyone out there plays an instrument you can relate and you can maybe know about these.
content.trans: 好的。那么，如果你们当中有人会乐器的话，应该能理解并知道这些吧。

content.text: These things that you may know in your original language. I know many people who play musical instruments and don't really know the technical words in their original language.
content.trans: 你知道你原语言中这些东西。我认识很多人会弹乐器，但其实对原语言中的技术词并不太熟悉。

content.text: I mean things like Andante and Pianissimo, things like this I think are universal, right? They're used in whatever language.
content.trans: 我指的是像Andante和Pianissimo这样的东西，我觉得这些应该是通用的吧？它们在任何语言中都用得着。

content.text: Exactly. Very widely used.
content.trans: 确实。非常广泛使用。

content.text: But things like the accidental or bass clef or scales and stuff like that I think it's obviously different languages.
content.trans: 但是像意外的或低音谱号或和声小调之类的，我觉得肯定是不同的语言。

content.text: For example, you know Italian like scales or accidentals. They're different.
content.trans: 例如，你知道意大利语就像音阶或装饰音一样。它们是不同的。

content.text: They're different, right? They're different. All of the other words. So the instructions on the page because music is shared all over the world.
content.trans:
当然不一样！所有的其他词都不一样。页面上的说明是因为音乐是全世界共享的。

输出 ONLY 翻译结果，无须解释。

content.text: The instructions on the page are almost always in Italian. So piano, Andante or they're in German.
content.trans: 页面上的说明几乎总是用意大利语、帕梯纳语或德语。

content.text: Oh really?
content.trans: 真的吗？

content.text: So music. But everything else, scales, octaves. These are all in your native language.
content.trans: 所以音乐。但是其他的一切，调子、八度音程。这些都是你的母语。

content.text: And so they're very, very important to study if you want to play. And I think very, very useful if you want to study an instrument.
content.trans: 所以如果你想玩游戏，一定要好好研究它们。如果你想要学习一种乐器，我觉得非常有用。

content.text: Yeah, of course. I think it's also very good idea to just have a general knowledge about these things.
content.trans: 当然，我觉得了解这些也很不错。

content.text: Because you know, sometimes it's nice to know a little bit about it. And maybe if a friend is talking about music,
content.trans: 因为你知道，有时候知道一些关于它的小知识也不错。说不定朋友聊音乐的时候能给你讲点新鲜事儿呢。

content.text: you can maybe understand a little bit more about what it's like. Or if you see music, a sheet of music, you can now more or less know what's going on with all those drawings and little scribbles.
content.trans: 你或许能稍微了解一些。或者，如果你看到音乐、一张乐谱或小草图，现在就差不多知道这些图画和小草的大部分内容了。

content.text: Absolutely. And if you have any questions of course, you're welcome to come to our website and ask or share your experiences as Marco has just said.
content.trans: 当然。如果你有任何问题，你大可以来我们网站上提问或分享你的经验，就像Marco刚才说的那样。

content.text: So please come to EnglishPod.com. We hope to see you there.
content.trans: 请来英语pod.com吧。我们期待在那里见到你。

content.text: All right. We'll see you guys next time. Bye.
content.trans: 好的。下次见你们。拜拜。
